findings.detail: The question repeats the problem of M2-S56-T1, only moved to a support agent. A high overall accuracy on a labeled set leads someone to a conclusion about every segment, and the same reasoning gives the answer: the aggregate can mask a weak segment, so check per segment. The wrong options also repeat the earlier set. A repeats 'approve because the overall figure is high'. B repeats 'make the overall estimate more precise or stable'. D repeats 'use model-reported confidence'. Three wrong options repeat, and at most one may.

blind_answer.reason: Aggregate accuracy can mask regressions in small segments: billing disputes are only 6% of the set, so they could get worse while the overall rate still rises. The claim should be checked by breaking accuracy down per request type (5.5-K1, 5.5-S2). Rerunning the full set only confirms the overall figure is stable, and self-reported confidence is not a reliable measure of correctness.
